A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMTok with matching authors, core equations, algorithms and benchmark experiments. All 21 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMTok benchmark results, component ablations, token-budget experiments and inference measurements, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds reasoning, resizing, runtime, decoder-pruning and implementation-fix experiments.

M1.justification: v2 removes the agent-assisted procedure in v1 Section 3.2. It introduces additional pruning at decoder layer 24 and MMTok++, which excludes padding patches and fixes token overflow (Appendices B.6 and C). These change the available inference procedures, although the central coverage objective and greedy algorithms remain unchanged; the main benchmarks explicitly retain the unfixed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMStar evaluation covering perception and several reasoning categories (Appendix B.3), plus a multi-turn visual-question-answering case using tokens selected for the first question (Figure 3). The existing benchmark coverage remains; most other additions use existing MME data.

E2.justification: Table 7 introduces image resizing alone as an explicitly evaluated token-reduction alternative. FastV, SparseVLM, VisionZip, fine-tuned VisionZip and DivPrune remain in their corresponding existing comparisons. The new MMStar experiment uses the already established VisionZip and DivPrune comparators.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design with resize-factor and retention grids, encoder-only versus layer-24 pruning controls, and timing measurements varying input and selected-token counts. It also introduces category-wise MMStar evaluation. Existing main benchmark settings largely remain unchanged; the revised ScienceQA scores do not establish an underlying protocol change.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained coverage, temperature and pooling ablations, v2 adds resizing/pruning combinations, runtime scaling, decoder-stage selection and a comparison incorporating padding and overflow fixes. Figures 3–5 add case studies of multi-turn reuse, question difficulty and semantic alignment of selected patches. The earlier agent-specific analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Table 13 first reports averaging runtime measurements over 100 runs. This concerns the new timing experiment, rather than an established increase in repetitions of existing experiments. Neither version provides accuracy confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds result sets in Tables 7 and 11–15 and removes MMTokAgent results. Existing ScienceQA values change, including full-token dynamic-resolution Qwen accuracy from 76.65 to 87.46. MMTok's LLaVA-NeXT high-IC average at an upper budget of 10 tokens changes from 79.9% to 71.0% (v1 Table 16; v2 Table 22), correcting aggregation of retained component scores. Section 4.3 also revises the stated multimodal ablation advantage from more than 5% to about 1%.

T1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds an O(kn) complexity claim and accompanying scaling argument for greedy selection. The coverage definitions, submodularity propositions, approximation guarantee, corollary and adaptive-temperature derivation remain unchanged; no new detailed proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The core multimodal-coverage and efficiency claims remain, including the 1.87× speedup with 98.7% performance retention. Agent-assisted text enrichment disappears from the abstract and introduction and becomes a future direction in the conclusion, narrowing the previously presented contribution.

C2.justification: v2 attributes multi-turn token reuse to vision-vision coverage, links required token budgets to question difficulty, and discusses combining resizing with selection. Appendix B.3 qualifies the reasoning evaluation by noting low full-model accuracy. The earlier explanation of failures from uninformative multiple-choice agent responses is removed.

D1.justification: v2 first supplies a MMTok code URL and release statement. It adds A6000 profiling information, PyTorch implementation remarks and disclosure of the padding/overflow fixes. The SmolVLM2-256M agent configuration is removed, while the principal temperature settings and evaluation-framework information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for MMStar, LLaVA-PruMerge and VisionThink, and removes the SmolVLM reference associated with the deleted agent variant. The central positioning of multimodal coverage against unimodal token-selection methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper receives localized prose editing, removal of the agent subsection, revised concluding directions and new ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. Appendices are reorganized around additional experiments and visualizations, but most existing exposition and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables and three substantive visualization figures. Figure 1 drops the agent series, Figure 2 is redrawn without the agent branch, and Tables 1–2 lose agent rows. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through resizing comparisons, reasoning evaluation and runtime analysis, while adding implementation-fix disclosure and a code-release pointer. Corrected high-IC averages and the moderated ablation statement improve reporting accuracy. The central evidence was already extensive in v1, and the ScienceQA revisions remain unexplained, so the overall gain is useful but limited.
